test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2024: Official Paper (Held On: 03 Jul, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In a right-angled triangle ABC such that ∠BAC = 90° and AD is perpendicular to BC. If the area of ΔABC is 63 cm², area of ΔACD = 7 cm², and AC = 5 cm, then the length of BC is equal to:
solution:
**Given:**

Area of ΔABC = 63 cm²

Area of ΔACD = 7 cm²

AC = 5 cm

**Formula used:**

If ΔABC ∼ ΔXYZ, then

ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔXYZ) = (AB/XY)² = (BC/YZ)2 = (AC/XZ)2

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb956877f6a76bd78a2be16fedfb79b974615ef705dee8dad8fe9661bd687061.png] 

In ΔABC and ΔACD

∠BAC = ∠ADC = 90° 

∠C = ∠C (Common in both triangles)

So, ΔABC ∼ ΔDAC (by AA Similarity)

Now,

ar(ΔABC) / ar(ΔACD) = (BC/AC)²

⇒ 63/7 = (BC/5)²

⇒ 9/1 = (BC/5)2

⇒ √(9/1) = BC/5

⇒ 3 = BC/5

⇒ BC = 5 × 3 = 15 cm

**∴ The length of BC is 15 cm**
